title: Admin bootstrap and rotation checks must read the primary DB, not the read replica
answers: basic-auth server fails to start with needs a password error after removing admin password
read replica lag makes admin user appear missing
has_user returns false on replica after restart
basic auth startup with read_database_uri fails
body:
Symptom: With a read replica configured, restarting a basic-auth server after the bootstrap password was removed can fail with "needs a password to create the admin user" even though the admin exists.
Root cause: has_user and authenticate_user in mlflow/server/auth/sqlalchemy_store.py ran with ManagedSessionMaker(read_only=True), so the existence and legacy-password checks could hit a lagging replica.
Fix pattern: Add a keyword-only use_primary flag to has_user and authenticate_user, and pass use_primary=True from the bootstrap and rotation path in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:create_admin_user. Request-path reads keep the replica.
Constraints: Only startup bootstrap and rotation reads need the primary; the default stays read-only. Any new startup check that reads admin state should pass use_primary=True.
applies: Auth store reads during bootstrap and rotation when read_database_uri is configured.
says: Server fails to start claiming admin needs a password even though admin exists
Basic auth server crashes on restart after removing the initial setup password
Administrator account appears missing during startup when using a database read replica
Server startup fails with administrator creation prompt after database password rotation
Prevent database replication lag from breaking user authentication checks at server launch
search: Startup bootstrap and password rotation checks in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:create_admin_user must read from the primary database instead of a read replica. Functions has_user and authenticate_user in mlflow/server/auth/sqlalchemy_store.py accept use_primary=True to bypass ManagedSessionMaker(read_only=True) when read_database_uri is configured. Request-path reads keep the read replica default, and only startup bootstrap or rotation checks pass use_primary=True.
